display.purpose: Page titles and the masthead. Stamped caps, never prose.

headline.purpose: Numbered form section titles, beside a typed red index.

title.purpose: Card titles, day-plan titles, the photo button.

lead.purpose: The single lead sentence on the home surface.

figure.purpose: Every quantity, kg, day count, percent, distance, date and code path. Tabular numerals.

label.purpose: Names a box or the value under it. Carbon blue, or manila on a dark band.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: The ruled box at rest. Paper sitting slightly down and right of the ground.

shadows.name: sheet-lifted
shadows.purpose: Hover on the three link cards at the foot of the home page. The only hover lift in the build.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The stamp press on the home waybill. Lands from above, over-presses, then settles.

motion.name: press-worn
motion.purpose: The worn impression presses slightly faster, under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: bar-fill
motion.purpose: The storage gauge bar when the receiving kitchen changes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the press is removed and all transitions collapse.

textures.name: claim-hatch
textures.purpose: The pending claim band in a storage gauge.

textures.name: perforation
textures.purpose: The 1px tear line that closes a stretch of the form.

narrative.overview:
Every page renders as one sheet of a multi-part form. Manila kraft carries the ground. Readings sit on near-white stock inside bordered boxes, each titled by a box number in a carbon-ink band. Decisions print as rotated rubber stamps in the right-hand column of a ruled table. The reader should feel they hold the receiving copy of a form, not a charity website.

The system is dense and administrative. Figures are typed and line up in columns. Prose is short and sits between boxes, never in a hero. No dark mode ships, on purpose: the user stands at a back door in daylight, and paper in daylight is light.

The North Star name above was derived from the build, not confirmed with the user. The palette is also provisional in one place: a teammate may supply brand colours later, and the signal red (`stamp`) and the carbon blue (`carbon`) are the first tokens to re-map if she does.
keyCharacteristics: Manila kraft ground with two low-contrast dot fields, at 7px and 3px.
Every reading sits in a ruled box. An empty box still shows its ruling.
Three faces with fixed roles: stamped caps, prose, typed figures.
Zero corner radius everywhere except the 2px stamp.
Decisions read as a word first and a colour second.

rules.name: The Small-Area Red Rule
rules.body: The signal red never fills a large area and never tints the ground. It ships as an outline, a figure, a hairline border, a 7-12% wash, or a badge-sized fill. On the waybill, exactly one line carries it, even when two items share the lowest day count.

rules.name: The Word-Not-Colour Rule
rules.body: Every decision states its word inside the stamp. The colour repeats the word, it never replaces it, so the surface still reads in greyscale and for a colour-blind reader.

rules.name: The Ground-Carries-Everything Rule
rules.body: Manila is the page, not an accent on white. No surface opts out of it, and there is no dark theme.

rules.name: The Typed Figure Rule
rules.body: Every figure on this surface is typed. Set it in Courier Prime with tabular-nums and tnum, so columns of numbers line up. A figure in Barlow is a bug.

rules.name: The Placard-Names-Things Rule
rules.body: Archivo Black names things: the product, the page, the section, the card, the stamped word. It never sets running prose and never sets a figure.

rules.name: The Hairline Seam Rule
rules.body: Adjacent cells in a strip are separated by a 1px seam, made with gap-px over a faint-ink background, never by a margin. The strip reads as one printed block divided by rules.

rules.name: The Tear-Line Rule
rules.body: A perforated 1px dashed line closes a stretch of the form. Use it where the document would physically tear, not as a decorative divider between every block.

rules.name: The Paper-On-Paper Rule
rules.body: The offset stays, because the sheet sits off the ground, but the blur is what makes it a shadow. A zero-blur hard offset block is a poster device, and this world is a document.

rules.name: The One Worn Stamp Rule
rules.body: Wear belongs to the event, never to the page. Exactly one stamp on a surface may wear, and it is the line with the lowest day count. The wear is a coarse fractal-noise mask plus a 0.5px ink spread, with the alpha row of the colour matrix at -0.32 1.06, so the thinnest part of the mark still prints at about three quarters strength. Past about -0.6 the stamp stops being legible, which trades the decision for a texture. Legibility wins.

dos: Do put every reading in a ruled box, and show the diagonal ruling when the box is empty.
Do set every figure in Courier Prime with tabular numerals.
Do title a dense box with the carbon-ink header band and its box number.
Do keep corners square (0 radius), with the single 2px stamp exception.
Do separate cells in a strip with a 1px hairline seam.
Do say the decision in a word inside the stamp, and let colour repeat it.
Do keep prose measures between 34ch and 78ch.
Do name a field with a typed carbon-blue label directly above it.
donts: Don't use a zero-blur hard offset shadow. The one shadow in this system is blurred, because this is a document and not a poster.
Don't flood an area with the signal red. It ships as an outline, a figure, a hairline, a 7-12% wash, or a badge-sized fill.
Don't paint two waybill lines red, and don't wear two stamps on one surface. Both halve the only signal the document has.
Don't add corner radius above 2px, and don't add a shadow value beyond the two in the vocabulary.
Don't set prose in Archivo Black, or a figure in Barlow.

Don't put a typed label above a page title where it names nothing. A field label names a box or the value under it. Above an h1 it is a kicker, and the build already carries five of those ("Section 01" through "Section 05").
Don't use a glyph or an icon-font character as an icon. Icons are drawn SVG at stroke-width: 1.75 with round caps.

Don't use numeric font-weight utilities (font-400, font-600, font-700). Tailwind v4.3.3 compiles them to nothing, so the weight is silently dropped and the text renders at 400. The build carried sixteen of them until they were found and replaced with font-normal, font-semibold and font-bold. Verify a weight in the built CSS before trusting it.
Don't add a dark theme. The user reads this in daylight, and paper in daylight is light.
